source_signature.notes: Batch 4E skill 2/6 — RETIRES the coulomb_friction_impending unsigned-prereq inversion. SCOPE WAS OPERATOR-DERIVED, not Architect-ruled: the Batch 4E ruling detailed skill 1/6's scope only while explicitly ordering this skill opened after contact_force_modeling signed. Scope derived from graph truth and the signed boundaries, and recorded here as such. The gap it fills is precise: dry_friction_static_kinetic (ca18a52a, parent) takes N as GIVEN — its prompt hands the student N = 250 N; contact_force_modeling (2ae7e45d, parent) PLACES N with magnitude explicitly unknown; coulomb_friction_impending (signed, downstream) CONSUMES N in the friction law. Nobody determined N's magnitude. This skill does, from normal-direction equilibrium only. Misconception owned: N is not the weight — students carry N = W from horizontal-surface problems, and a wrong N silently corrupts every downstream friction calculation because N is the friction law's input. Duplicate hazard against the signed friction_equilibrium_sliding cleared at the review beat: that skill selects mu_k or mu_s, writes BOTH force equations, and solves a full sliding or verge problem; this one writes the normal equation only and stops. Four hard stops verified absent from every step: no mu*N, no static/kinetic/impending regime, no tangential solve, no 3D. Worked example independently re-derived by Operator: block W = 100 N on a rough plane at 36.9 degrees (cos 0.80, sin 0.60), applied force P = 50 N perpendicular into the plane; SumFn = 0 gives N - 80 - 50 = 0, N = 130 N, and N = 130 does not equal W = 100. This is the multi-parent composition case (prereq_n = 2), and Architect Batch 4E Decision B governs: canonical four only, signals mapped to authored procedural steps. 3-signal mapping, content-earned: axis_confusion at step 3 (resolving weight and applied forces onto surface-aligned axes) — this is the skill's OWN contribution, since neither parent has a resolution step; sign_or_placement_error at step 4 (writing the normal equilibrium equation); unclassified at step 6 (reporting and scope boundary). simple_average_used omitted: Centroids-family signal. Review-beat correction: the original example used P = 40 N, under which the sine/cosine swap (axis_confusion at step 3) gave W sin theta + P = 100 N and the N = W error (named in sign_or_placement_error at step 4's own trigger) ALSO gave 100 N — two distinct signals collided on one wrong answer, so a student reporting 100 N could not be routed to the right remediation. P changed to 50 N, separating all four paths: correct 130, sine/cosine swap 110, N = W 100, omitted P 80. Same defect family as the symmetric load on general_distributed_load_resultant, the inclined force at the moment centre on rigid_body_equilibrium_2d, and the single rough interface on contact_force_modeling — applied to signal DISCRIMINATION rather than signal liveness. The symbol f was also declared: it does real work in this skill's solution steps, unlike mu_s and mu_k, which appear only where they name the ruled-out boundary and are correctly left undeclared.
